ledger.claim: Recorded distances establish the deviation: the trip ran 11.4 km against a recommended route of 10.0 km, a deviation of 1.40 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so this is a deviation the POL-RD-24 matrix must price rather than excuse.

The driver-device trace independently shows which route was taken: the vehicle is on Bendemeer Road from 19:00:44 through 19:05:14, between the recorded deviation at the CTE/Bendemeer Road exit at 19:00:36 and the rejoin at Upper Serangoon Road/Braddell Road at 19:11:06, so the departure from the recommended route is not in issue and lasted roughly ten and a half minutes.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The clause requires a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route, and the platform's own derived reading of the LTA advisory records intersects_route as null and states 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route', with the question left undetermined. An advisory whose intersection with the recommended route is undetermined does not show an incident on the recommended route segment at the trip time, and the driver's own in-app assertion of a jam (EV-CHAT-05003) cannot supply that link - POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. Row (d) of POL-RD-24 therefore applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full.

The refund row (d) provides is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, with no surge: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.008 SGD, rounded to the cent, 1.01 SGD. The claim text asks for 4.50 SGD, but POL-RD-24 gives no route to more than the excess distance fare, so the rider's case is made out as a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD, not the full 4.50 SGD.

The driver's stated justification - that the Bendemeer route 'should be faster' and 'was faster than sitting in the jam' (his chat message and his counter-statement) - is not borne out by the trip record, which shows the trip at 23.0 minutes against the recommended route's 20.2 minutes. A reroute the rider got no benefit from is not one that POL-RD-23 lets the driver's own say-so carry.

If the judge is not prepared to find the traffic question either way, POL-GEN-26 governs the case: whether traffic justified the reroute is a fact POL-RD-23 needs, and on this record it cannot be established, because the platform's own derived assessment leaves the advisory's intersection with the recommended route undetermined. The case then goes to human review with the amount held rather than left with the rider.

Even if a traffic justification is found, row (a) of POL-RD-24 does not close the case: it requires that the rider was 'informed and agreed', and the rider's only message is 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' - a bare acknowledgment of the reason given, not agreement to bear 1.40 km of extra metered distance. Where the rider is informed but has not agreed to the extra charge, the case fits no row of POL-RD-24 and is escalated under POL-GEN-26 rather than refused.

The recorded distances fix the deviation at 1.40 km: trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.40 km less optimal_distance_km 10.00 km. That is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the deviation is over tolerance and POL-RD-24's matrix is engaged. The trace is not used to re-measure the distance (POL-RD-22); the platform's recorded distances are, and they are complete.

The reroute is traffic-justified on this record. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260805-1205 is an ACCIDENT, which POL-RD-23's traffic_justification_types maps to the admissible 'incident' limb; its road is the Central Expressway (CTE), a road named on the recommended route in trip_record.optimal_route_via and in the trip_started event; and its validity window 18:37:44-19:49:44 covers the trip window 18:49:44-19:12:44. The advisory the driver described to the rider is the advisory in the record.

The driver gave notice before the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. Driver message MSG-05003-003 ('CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster.') was sent at 18:57:46 and delivered at 18:57:48; the platform's route_deviation_detected event fires at 19:00:36, roughly three minutes later. The notice is in-app chat, which is the channel POL-RD-21 names.

The rider acknowledged the notice, so the deviation is agreed under POL-RD-21. MSG-05003-004, sent by the rider at 18:58:26 and read at 18:58:49, reads 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' — a confirmed acknowledgment in the chat log. The driver's counterparty statement ('I told the passenger in the app before I exit... he said ok') matches the log entry for entry, and the log is contiguous at weight 1.0.

Row (a) of POL-RD-24 applies, and exactly one row applies. The reroute is traffic-justified (POL-RD-23); the rider was informed by in-app chat before the deviation and acknowledged it (POL-RD-21); and the deviation is over 1 km (1.40 km, POL-RD-22). Row (a) returns no refund. The rider's claim is therefore not supported and the present state stands: NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03, with the charged fare of 22.60 SGD untouched.

Even if the case were to fall on a refund row, the rider's figure is not the policy's figure. POL-RD-24 caps the refund at the excess distance fare: deviation 1.40 km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, without surge, rounded to the cent — 1.01 SGD. The claim for 4.50 SGD is more than four times any amount POL-RD-24 can award, so the rider cannot be entitled to the whole contested sum on any row.

No threshold sends this case away from the AI. The contested amount is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band in which the AI ruling is final; the driver profile carries fraud_flags 0, so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift does not bite; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false, and 1.40 km would clear it in any event). The ruling should issue as NO_ACTION rather than being escalated.

In the alternative, if and only if the judge cannot resolve whether the advisory's CTE segment is the recommended route's CTE segment, then whether traffic justified the reroute is a fact the record cannot establish, and POL-GEN-26 governs it: the case goes to human review rather than being decided against the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the charged fare stands pending review — preferable to a refund the record does not support.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver. WHAT IS AGREED. The recommended route was 10.00 km and the trip as driven was 11.40 km (EV-TRIP-05003). The deviation is therefore 1.40 km (POL-RD-22), above the 1.00 km tolerance, and neither side disputes it; the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05003) shows the same movement, the vehicle leaving the CTE at Bendemeer Road at 19:00:36 and rejoining at Upper Serangoon Road/Braddell Road at 19:11:06. WAS THE REROUTE TRAFFIC-JUSTIFIED? Yes (POL-RD-23). The LTA traffic advisory in the record (EV-ADVIS-05003-01, weight 1.0, complete) reports an accident on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which covers this trip's 18:49:44-19:12:44 window. The recommended route in the trip record runs along the CTE towards SLE (optimal_route_via), and the platform's own deviation event records that the recommended route at the point the driver left it was the CTE. The accident therefore lies on that CTE stretch, in the direction of travel, inside the trip window, and the advisory intersects the recommended route. The rider is right that the platform's derived reading left this 'undetermined' and the record does not decide it for the parties, but POL-RD-23 asks the decision to be made from the advisory's road, direction and location against the trip, and on those it does intersect. I do not find this a fact the record cannot establish, and I decline to escalate on the rider's POL-GEN-26 ground, and equally on the driver's alternative request to escalate on the same point. WAS THE RIDER INFORMED AND DID THE RIDER AGREE? Yes (POL-RD-21). The driver's in-app message MSG-05003-003 ('CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster.', EV-CHAT-05003) was sent 18:57:46 and read 18:58:03, about three minutes before the 19:00:36 deviation. The rider replied MSG-05003-004 ('Ok sure, thanks for telling') at 18:58:26, read 18:58:49. The rider argues this is a bare acknowledgment, not agreement to 1.40 km of extra metered distance. POL-RD-21 answers it: where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed. The log confirms it, so the deviation was agreed, and the case does not fall outside POL-RD-24's rows on that ground. WHICH ROW (POL-RD-24). Exactly one row applies. Traffic-justified; rider informed and agreed; deviation over 1.00 km: row (a), no refund. The rider's claim for 4.50 SGD is not supported. For completeness, the refund rows would have capped recovery at the excess distance fare: 1.40 km x the 0.72 SGD per km rate = 1.01 SGD, without surge, far below the 4.50 SGD claimed and against a 22.60 SGD fare; the rider's own advocate conceded that figure. The driver's point that no row could award 4.50 SGD is correct but does not arise. The rider's further point that the reroute was not actually faster (23.0 minutes against the recommended 20.2 minutes) is accurate but immaterial: POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute on the traffic data, not on whether it saved time. DECISION (POL-GEN-03). The rider filed, so the ruling is read against the rider's claim. That claim is not supported and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, no refund, no driver compensation, and no money moves - the 22.60 SGD fare already charged stands. WHO DECIDES (POL-RD-25, POL-GEN-22). The contested value is 4.50 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band; the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 0, so the 0.95 uplift does not bite; the route-deviation bar is 0.80 and this ruling is issued at 0.85. The AI's 2 km deviation limit is not applied (thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), and 1.40 km would clear it in any event. No safety flag applies, and a route deviation carries no referral clause, so there is no referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
